# Key messages for donors (auto-generated from the data)

1. 55% of organisation-based helpers report moderate or high burnout (self-employed: 29%).
2. 73% of highly burned-out helpers seriously consider leaving at least monthly, versus 21% of those with low burnout.
3. A heavy workload goes with more burnout; enthusiasm for the work and good organisational support go with less.
4. Largest support gaps (staff want it, organisation lacks it): Career development (36%) and Acting-position allowance (35%).
5. Staff and leaders differ by 10+ points on 4 of 8 supports (only 28 leaders answered).
6. 3% of staff expect leaders to be enthusiastic about a support programme; 27% of leaders say they are. 38% of staff expect leaders to see it as unnecessary or ill-timed, versus 9% of leaders.
7. Frontline staff have the fewest job resources and the highest burnout: job resources 57/100 and burnout 58/100 for frontline staff.
8. Self-employed helpers average 42/100 on burnout versus 53 in organisations, and 78 versus 57 on enthusiasm for work.
9. Unstable income is named by 69% of self-employed helpers among their top three challenges.

*All figures: volunteer sample; they describe the people who answered and show what goes together, not what causes what.*
